threads.body: `pyproject_reqs` is a set, so iterating it here produces nondeterministic error ordering across runs/Python versions. Sorting makes CI output stable and easier to diff when multiple requirements are missing bounds.

threads.body: The new instruments constraint `langchain >= 0.3.21, < 1` conflicts with this package’s own test matrix: `instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-langchain/tests/requirements.latest.txt` pins `langchain==1.3.15` (line 17). With the extra capped to `< 1`, the editable install `...-langchain[instruments]` cannot resolve alongside the pinned 1.x dependency and will fail the `*-latest` env. Either widen the supported range (e.g. `< 2` if 1.x is supported) or update the tests/README to stop targeting 1.x.

The suggested upper-bound example `'< (x+1)'` is not a valid PEP 508 specifier and may confuse contributors copy/pasting it. Consider using a syntactically valid placeholder like `'< 2'` or `'< next_major'`.

@@ -162,6 +163,22 @@ def check_instruments_match(pkg_dir: Path, pyproject: dict) -> list[str]:
             f"does not match pyproject.toml instruments extra ({pyproject_instruments_raw})."
         )
 
+    for req in pyproject_reqs:
+        has_lower = any(
+            s.operator in (">=", ">", "~=", "==") for s in req.specifier
+        )
+        has_upper = any(
+            s.operator in ("<", "<=", "~=", "==") for s in req.specifier
+        )
+        if not has_lower:
+            errors.append(
+                f"{pkg_dir.name}: requirement '{req}' in pyproject.toml instruments extra is missing a lower bound (e.g. '>= x.y.z')."
+            )
+        if not has_upper:
+            errors.append(
+                f"{pkg_dir.name}: requirement '{req}' in pyproject.toml instruments extra is missing an upper bound (e.g. '< (x+1)')."
+            )

threads.body: `_instruments` is now capped at `langchain < 1`, but this repo’s langchain instrumentation tests explicitly pin `langchain==1.3.15` (see `instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-langchain/tests/requirements.latest.txt:17`). This cap will prevent resolving/installing the test env (and can also cause the runtime compatibility check to reject supported 1.x installs).

The README now advertises `langchain >= 0.3.21, < 1`, but the langchain instrumentation’s own `tests/requirements.latest.txt` pins `langchain==1.3.15`. Unless support for 1.x is being dropped (and the tests updated accordingly), this documentation bound is inconsistent with the tested supported versions.
